Appearance:
MR JK SHAH, APP for the PETITIONER(s) No. 1,2,3 RULE SERVED(64) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 1,2,3 ==========================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE B.N. KARIA  Date : 22/04/2018  ORAL ORDER 1.

This Criminal Appeal preferred under Section 378 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is directed against the judgment and order of acquittal dated 31.10.2012 passed by learned 3rd Additional Sessions Judge, Jamnagar in Criminal Appeal No. 25/2008, acquitting the respondents for an offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
2. This Appeal is taken up for settlement in Lok Adalat.
3. Mr. J. K. Shah, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has appeared on behalf of the State and has produced withdrawal / settlement pursis, which is taken on record.

The withdrawal / settlement pursis is signed by the authorized signatory, who is R/CR.A/99/2014 ORDER present in person before this Lok Adalat and the pursis is counter signed by learned APP and respective learned advocates.
Original complainant Shri A.B. Ghelani, Food Inspector is not present.

However, on a pursis, Shri C.S. Gohil has put his signature as an authorized person, which is duly identified by Mr.
D.R. Sharma, Law Officer of the Department.
Shri Sharma is present before the Court.
He stated that whatever the order will be passed will be binding to him and he has no objection to the compromise.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the offence alleged against the accused under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, is not serious in nature, the penalty / punishment prescribed for such offence is not substantial in view of the Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.
5. In view of the withdrawal / compromise pursis of the parties, this Appeal stands disposed of.

The respondent No. 2 is directed to pay a sum of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand Only) and respondents No.1 and 3 are directed to pay a sum of Rs. 3,000/- (Rupees Three thousand only) each (in all, the respondent No. 2 to pay Rs. 5,000/- and respondents No. 1 and 3 to pay Rs. 6,000/-)
towards litigation cost, as agreed between the parties, in lieu thereof.
Necessary cost be deposited in the office of the High Court Legal Service Committee within four weeks, failing which the R/CR.A/99/2014 ORDER Appeal shall stand revived automatically.
Accordingly, this appeal stands disposed of.

6. However, disposal of this matter will not affect any connected matters arising out of the same,
incidental or any other proceedings, filed or to be filed before any other Court.
It is also required to be noted that this order will not be treated as a precedent in any future case for reference.
